questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose a country I would't otherwise visit. I wanted to be better at English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You can find the information but it takes a lot of time to get everything in order before your stay. Some time you wait a long time for people to answer you. Start in good time

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They send a couple of email. You need to know where to get help yourself, but when I figured that out they where helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find it easily. If you want off campus housing it's a good idea to se the place before signing anything. Places can differ from pictures, people can scam you or the place can be very dirty

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was glad living in the city, the housing on campus is very expensive. But mostly because I was only studying to days a week in campus, so I found it nice to live in the city and close to where thing happen. But I think it would be fun living on campus as well, it may depend on age and if your master or bachelor. I feel like most people are BA on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't look that much into it just thought it was expensive also because it's a little out of the city

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was just a form

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can email and chat with people

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took some time to figure out how to register and enroll but when you figure it out it's vey smart that you can choose different timeslots and plan your school hours in a better way. If you take popular classes it's smart to be ready to enroll in classes the day it opens, so you can get the good timeslots

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early because it takes a lot of time to get everything in order. Some of the information emails arrive later than you need them. SO there are some videos to explain things

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took some classes I'm not used to so I don't have anything to compare with. I liked my classes

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level in general is a little bit easier than KU. But I still learned a lot as it was in english

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were mandatory classes. Assignments that count in your final grade throughout the semester. Classes were based more on peoples experiences I'm more used to the teacher talking with evidence behind statements

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Health and Well-being in Early Childhood
- Families in Context
- Understanding Child Development: Infants and Young Children
- Healthy Places: Planning for Diversity, Equity and Wellbeing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I likes them all. These Understanding Child Development: Infants and Young Children and Healthy Places: Planning for Diversity, Equity and Wellbeing the most

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of activities and clubs you can join

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I thinks is always fun to join a club and some parties

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to talk to random people a school the first days and on the introduction days. They are also there to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That it was easier find friends that were also international students than the locals, at least of you are only there for one semester

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are so nice and so friendly!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go travel and see the different part of the Australia. Arrange your schedule so you have maybe to or three days in a row, so you have the possibility to travel the other days

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: MQ is a little out of the city, but it only takes 25 min by metro, so it didn't matter to me

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Thinking you need to says yes to everything. You don't, if your are there for a long time you definitely need off-days

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
